answer: Each of 192 aliases needs its own trademark records, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The dune is the wall and the umber is the gate: A trademark ownership tenure with registry renewals works as the gate: a mark renewed with the registry every ten years. A farm of 192 aliases must climb the wall 192 times, the karst ledger shows every climb, and one honest agent walks through the gate once.
